randomized_v1_v2_equivalence.note: Both versions used the same 40-step water-filling root and 50-step endpoint inversion; V2 changes storage/merge representation only.

batch_reference_scope.earlier_validation: V1 already matched the frozen batch breakpoint solver to about 1e-12 endpoint tolerance over hundreds of prefixes. Exact V1/V2 numerical equality therefore carries that implementation comparison forward under the same floating-point path.
batch_reference_scope.do_not_overclaim: This is transitive implementation evidence, not an independent mathematical proof.

tracemalloc_build_stress.scope: One local Python research runtime. tracemalloc overhead is substantial; use only as relative prototype evidence, not production memory/latency.

design_change.removed: Duplicated raw lower/upper tuple payload retained alongside sorted threshold and suffix arrays.
design_change.retained: Per-item threshold/lconst arrays plus suffix aggregates, so merges do not reconstruct individual values from large suffix differences.
design_change.reason: A more aggressive suffix-difference-only prototype reduced memory further but can amplify floating-point cancellation during merges. V2 intentionally keeps per-item lconst/sat arrays for numerical stability.

remaining_bottleneck: Endpoint queries still perform fixed numerical root bisection across O(log n) immutable runs. Next optimization should target root lookup/warm-start/query caching without weakening fail-closed numerical residual checks.
scope_guards: V2 is a computational/storage refactor only.
The 27.2% peak-memory and 23.0% build-time reductions are local prototype measurements.
Do not remove per-item arrays solely for memory until cancellation error is bounded or compensated summation is added and revalidated.
